newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: OECD sees Austria 1997 GDP growth at 1.4 pct.
newsitem.headline: OECD sees Austria 1997 GDP growth at 1.4 pct.

text.p: Austria's economy is poised for "moderate growth" of 1.4 percent for 1997, and should be able to cut its budget deficit to three percent of GDP this year, the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development said on Thursday.
In its latest report the Paris-based think tank predicted strong private consumption would cause an acceleration of Austrian GDP growth to 2.3 percent in 1998. GDP grew 1.1 percent in 1996.
Austria's budget deficit in relation to GDP should fall to three percent in 1997 from 4.3 percent last year, but could rise to 3.4 percent in 1998, the OECD continued.

Austria has passed austerity budgets for both 1996 and 1997 in a bid to bring its excessive budget deficit down to the three percent of GDP stipulated by the Maastricht criteria for European economic and monetary union.
The OECD forecast a slight decline in the jobless rate for 1998 to 6.4 percent from an expected 6.5 percent in 1997 and 6.2 percent in 1996.
